label: Leipäjuusto
note: Traditionally made from reindeer milk; today usually cow milk, preferably the first milk (colostrum) after calving, or goat

about.text: Bread cheese, sometimes known in the United States as Finnish squeaky cheese, is a Finnish fresh cheese traditionally made from cow's colostrum. In the US, cow's milk is generally used but can also be made with goat milk. Commercially available versions are typically made from cow's milk. The cheese originally comes from Southern Ostrobothnia, Northern Finland, and Kainuu.

how.label: bake
how.text: A fresh rennet curd is spread into a thin sheet and baked on both sides until dark-spotted; the heat firms the squeaky curd and browns its surface, and the cheese is ready to eat straight after baking.
